newsitem.title: UK: Euro bourses rattled by Wall St volatility.
newsitem.headline: Euro bourses rattled by Wall St volatility.

text.p: European stocks clawed back some losses on Thursday but remained below the record levels set the previous day, rattled by Wall Street's uncertain opening.
On currency markets, the dollar climbed strongly, rising against the mark on weak German jobs data and hitting a new four-year high of 124 yen at one point.
In London, shares fell back as investors waited to see if Wall Street could recoup some of the sharp losses suffered on Wednesday. New York slipped in and out of profit at its opening on Thursday.
Steady UK interest rates helped calm jittery market nerves which dealers said could still snap if U.S. jobless figures, due on Friday, show the U.S. economy is still steaming ahead.
"We're once again waiting on the U.S. non-farm payrolls," one senior dealer said.
"If we get a rogue number -- something way out of line-- this rally could be over."
The FTSE 100 was down 0.4 percent in early afternoon. The index closed at a new peak of 4281.5 points on Wednesday as optimism grew that interest rates would hold steady.
The FTSE has risen four percent so far this year, reaching many analysts' year-end target levels as recent economic data on both sides of the Atlantic indicated inflation was still under control.

Both UK and U.S. interest rates were left on hold after monetary meetings on Wednesday but investors feared a strong U.S. unemployment report for January would increase chances of a U.S. interest rate hike next month, triggering a slide in bond and share markets.
Most economists believe UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke is anxious to avoid tightening monetary policy in the run-up to the looming UK election.

Wednesday saw the Dow's weakest finish since January 23, when U.S. blue chips slumped 94 points at the start of a five-session decline. The Dow's fall occurred despite news that the U.S. central bank's policy-making body had left interest rates unchanged at its two-day meeting that ended on Wednesday.
In Paris, shares regained some poise after opening sharply lower following Wall Street's overnight drop.

Cie Generale des Eaux and Havas were suspended pending a statement. The two companies will hold a joint news conference starting at 1630 GMT where they are expected to announce a deal concerning their stakes in satellite broadcaster Canal Plus .
In Frankfurt, stocks slipped in and out profit but closed just in the plus column as the higher-than-expected jobless figures were seen as keeping interest rates in check.
On the foreign exchange front, the dollar was firm, its sentiment strong after gaining on the mark on weak German jobs data and hitting a new four-year high of 124 yen.

But traders said the dollar was likely to tread water for now or even ease slightly as it had no fresh incentive to put on more weight, and also because U.S. non-farm payrolls data were due out on Friday.
The dollar had leapt higher as German government figures showed unemployment surged by over a half a million in January to a new post-war record of 4.66 million.
The unemployment rate, which is based on unadjusted data, rose to 12.2 percent, compared with 10.8 percent in December.

"The report is certainly going to keep dollar/mark well bid. Going into the G7, it would look a bit odd if the current weakness of the numbers in Germany and Japan made the G7 able to feel able to do much about the dollar's rise," said Chris Turner, currency strategist at BZW in London.
The dollar was up nearly half a pfennig at one point before falling back slightly. It was also stronger against the yen.

The jobless data set the tone for a day of strong trading for the dollar, with analysts seeing little reason to sell it off except some profit-taking and perhaps a little wariness ahead of the Group of Seven (G7) meeting in Berlin this weekend.

"Weak unemployment figures...would reinforce speculation of monetary easing in Germany, and that should give the dollar a bit of a bid against the mark," said Nigel Richardson, international economist at Yamaichi International.
CURRENCIES AT 1545 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6503 marks and 123.60 yen compared with 1.6479 marks and 123.54 yen in late European trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1545 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was 14.4 points down at 4267.1.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 6.14 at 3104.14.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 14.25 at 2,555.50.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $342.80 an ounce compared with $342.95 at the close on Wednesday.
